newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bulgarian president for early elections - interview.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian president for early elections - interview.

text.p: Bulgarian President Zhelyu Zhelev was quoted on Saturday as saying early elections were the only way out of the major crisis now shaking his country.
"One can only hope to get out of the very serious situation with which we are confronted by organising early elections," Zhelev told the Paris newspaper Le Monde.
"Our country needs reforms which should be far more wide-ranging than those proposed by current political forces," he said.

The interview was published as opposition protesters determined to break the ex-communist ruling party's grip on power clashed with police in Sofia after security forces broke up a 10-hour siege of parliament.
An opposition leader there said crisis talks between Zhelev and political and security chiefs, including opposition leaders, had ended without agreement.
In his interview Zhelev said "the first thing we must do is amend the constitution because if economic transition has failed, it is partly because the regime's workings are no longer suitable".
"Bulgaria is a parliamentary republic like those which existed in Europe between the world wars. What we need is a semi-presidential regime like that which exists in France."
"In Bulgaria, people are famished and without hope. Everything is possible and the conduct of the population is impossible to predict," Zhelev said.
Riot police used clubs to break up a 10-hour opposition siege of parliament early on Saturday in the worst violence in the country since the collapse of one-party communist rule.

The confrontation, spurred by acute economic crisis, came after the governing Socialist Party refused to vote on Friday on a motion calling for fresh elections. The opposition UDF party walked out and urged a nationwide strike and civil disobedience.
